map.Shell 对空白极其敏感：if [ ... ] 里方括号两侧必须有空格、变量赋: Shell is extremely whitespace-sensitive: in `if [ ... ]` the brackets need spaces on both sides, variable assignment must have no spaces around `=`, and a line-continuation `\` must have nothing after it (including spaces). A formatter that doesn't know these rules can break the script. So after formatting, run shellcheck and actually run it in a test environment before going live.

map.按行遍历脚本并维护缩进深度与 case 块计数。先用「剥离引号、转义与行内注释后: Iterate line by line while tracking indent depth and a case-block counter. Heredocs are detected on a code-only view of each line (quotes, escapes and inline comments replaced by spaces): a line with << plus a delimiter opens heredoc mode, the delimiter line itself is emitted at the current indent, and every following line is preserved verbatim (indenting the body would change shell semantics) until a line equal to the delimiter closes it; << inside strings or comments never triggers it. Ordinary lines are trimmed and emitted; consecutive blank lines collapse to one. The current line's output depth drops by 1 (never below 0) when it is fi/done/esac, starts with a closing brace, starts with else/elif/then/do, or is a ;;/;&/;;& terminator. After emitting, the state depth drops by 1 for fi/done/esac, closing braces and terminators; stays unchanged for else/elif/then/do (the preceding if/for already opened a level); rises by 1 for lines starting with if/for/while/until/case, ending with an opening brace, or consisting only of an opening brace; and rises by 1 for a case branch pattern only inside a case block and only when the ) ends the line with no whitespace, quote or parenthesis before it. Output joins indent unit x output depth with the trimmed line. Minify trims each line and drops blank lines while preserving line breaks and never inserting semicolons; validation counts keywords and brackets on the stripped code and writes its report to the status bar without overwriting the output.
